title: Converged metrics ingestion for inference KPIs and cardinality-safe exports
creator: Aisha Fernandez
description: Goal: Build a single ingestion pipeline that accepts Prometheus scrape data and OpenTelemetry (OTel) metrics/traces, enriches and normalizes them into a small set of production inference KPIs, and exports both low-cardinality aggregates to our Prometheus/TSDB and high-cardinality detail to long-term storage. KPIs include per-model request latency percentiles (p50/p90/p99), tokens-generated-per-second, KV cache hit rate, active-models-per-tenant, and request error-rate. Pipeline must enforce cardinality limits, preserve resource/model semantics, and provide exemplar linking from histograms to traces for debugging regression events.
progress_updates: 2024-11-01: RFC drafted outlining consolidated OTel Collector topology with prometheus_receiver + metrics_transform + attribute_enricher + prometheus_exporter + routed_remote_write for high-cardinality sinks.

2024-11-06: POC: deployed collector with prometheus_receiver and metrics_transform, successfully normalized inference_request_duration_seconds from 3 different microservices. Load-tested to 15k scrapes/s on a single m5.xlarge equivalent; CPU dominated by label processing.

2024-11-10: Implemented deterministic model-version hashing and label bucketing to reduce cardinality of model_version tag. Initial integration PR filed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/482

2024-11-14: Added exemplars into histogram pipeline using trace_id mapping; validated exemplar->trace jump in Grafana panel. Manual review with Observability SRE completed; feedback: cap exemplar rate to 0.5% of requests to control trace volume.

2024-11-18: Integration tests added for tenant-scoped aggregation and for fallback routing to ClickHouse for high-cardinality metrics. Dashboard prototypes created at https://grafana.redwood-internal/d/inf-metrics/Inference-KPIs
2024-11-20: Load test 48h run: metrics ingestion stable at 120k labels/s after enabling batch processor and a label-filtering stage. Next: finalize alerting rules and rollout plan.
2024-11-21: Security reviewed instrumentation guidance; flagged removal of free-form user_id labels (Sanitization required).
acceptance_criteria: Canonical metric names and label schema documented and published to Confluence: inference.metrics.naming
Collector topology deployed to staging with prometheus_receiver + metrics_transform + batch + routed_remote_write
Per-model p50/p90/p99 latency and tokens/sec exported to Prometheus/TSDB at 1m rollup without >5% data loss
Exemplar links present for histogram buckets and open trace in <5s when clicking from Grafana
Cardinality throttling enforced: tenant+model+route cardinality under configured budget; high-cardinality routed to long-term store
Alert rules for ingestion backpressure, missing model metrics, and cache hit regressions in place with runbooks
Documentation and instrumentation guide published; at least two services updated to new resource attributes (redwood.model.name, redwood.model.version, redwood.tenant.id)
Performance: collector CPU < 60% at expected peak load for staging cluster size
notes: Metric naming conventions: use snake_case, unit suffixes (e.g., inference_request_duration_seconds, inference_tokens_generated_total)
Prefer histograms with exemplar support for latency and request-size; use explicit bucket boundaries tuned to model latencies (10ms, 50ms, 100ms, 250ms, 500ms, 1s, 2s, 5s)
Resource attributes required: redwood.model.name, redwood.model.version, redwood.tenant.id, redwood.deployment.zone
Avoid free-form user identifiers and request IDs as metric labels; use set-valued label 'request_type' and hashed request class when necessary
Cardinality strategy: deterministic hashing for model_version -> model_version_bucket (8 buckets) + aggregate label 'model_version_bucket' to maintain useful signal while bounding unique series
Trace sampling policy: parent-based with rules: always sample errors and requests >2s, 0.5% uniform sampling otherwise; exemplars capped to 0.5% of requests
Export plan: low-cardinality aggregates -> Prometheus remote_write/Thanos, high-cardinality -> ClickHouse/LongTermStore with TTL 90d
Retention tiers: 1m rollups for 90d in Prometheus, raw high-cardinality events to LTS for 365d
Exemplar linking: use trace_id in exemplar and ensure trace ingestion window aligns with metric batching to keep trace queryable for at least 10 mins after metric ingestion
comments: Marco Liu (2024-11-05): 'POC looks promising. Need clear fallback if Collector becomes bottleneck — recommend router with discard policy + telemetry of dropped series.'
Priya Shah (SRE, 2024-11-07): 'Agree on deterministic bucketing. Please add dashboards showing cardinality-by-label to detect regressions fast.'
Design review (2024-11-12): 'Converged topology approved with condition: add config knob to disable exemplar injection in low-memory envs.'
Security (2024-11-20): 'Sanitization required: drop user-provided strings from labels. Add linting check in CI for forbidden label keys.'
Marco Liu (2024-11-21): 'Next steps: schedule canary rollout to 3 services (runtime proxy, request-router, batcher) and measure CPU/cost delta. Create runbook for dropped-metrics incident.'
